title: The Printing Clone
goal: Printing never needs ownership. Zero clones.
hints: &user.clone() clones the String, then borrows the temporary - an allocation that lives for one call.
Both functions take &str already. Just lend the original.
explanation: The functions were designed correctly - they take &str. The caller ruins it with `&user.clone()`: manufacture a fresh String, borrow it for the call, drop it. The borrow of the clone works exactly as well as a borrow of the original - so `&user` twice does the same job with zero allocations. Clone-then-borrow is the most common clone smell in real code.
